s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, ST-segment elevations, and PR-segment depression on ECG, consistent with myocardial and pericardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and elevated inflammatory markers, consistent with pericardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, normal coronary arteries, and signs of inflammation, consistent with myocardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and chest pain, although normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely

shortlist.label: Coronary arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers and normal coronary arteries, consistent with inflammation of the coronary arteries

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated troponin, and ST-segment elevations on ECG, along with the absence of coronary artery disease on angiography, suggests an inflammatory process. The presence of pericarditic features (ST-segment elevations, PR-segment depression) and myocarditic features (elevated troponin) supports the diagnosis of myopericarditis, which is an inflammation of both the myocardium and pericardium.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: While pericarditic features are present, the elevated troponin suggests myocardial involvement, making myopericarditis a more comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: Myocarditis alone does not fully explain the pericarditic features (ST-segment elevations, PR-segment depression) seen on ECG.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Coronary arteritis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of coronary artery inflammation or damage on coronary angiography.
